runs.text: This is the same OGF and coefficient-extraction convention used in the Sequences, Series & Recurrences section.
An OGF records the number or weight a_n of size-n objects as the coefficient of x^n. It may be manipulated as a formal power series without choosing a numerical value of x.
Addition represents a disjoint choice of classes. Multiplication combines independently chosen components while adding their sizes, producing the Cauchy convolution.

items.text: State whether size begins at 0 and include the empty object when its coefficient is intended to be 1.
A product adds component sizes; it does not multiply matching coefficients term by term.
Formal identities are coefficientwise; numerical convergence matters only after substituting a value for x.
Use an EGF rather than an OGF when factorial normalization is required for labeled products.

A factor must encode every allowed contribution and exclude every forbidden one.
Bounds such as at most q replace an infinite geometric factor by a finite polynomial.
